A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same predictive-sufficiency framework and share identifiable experiments. All pages, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, are readable and support comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original transformer-probing experiments on conjugate distributions, hidden Markov models and rectangle hypothesis spaces, including posterior-moment, distribution-shift and memorization analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical studies and adds original topic-model experiments, natural-corpus evaluations, controls, architecture sweeps and statistical analyses.

M1.justification: The central autoregressive representation-learning and probing procedure is retained, including linear-softmax probes and nonlinear variants already present in v1. Topic applications, different model configurations and the auxiliary reverse-prediction MLP expand the experiments without revising the core learning or inference method.

E1.justification: V2 retains the original synthetic tasks and adds LDA-generated documents, partially exchangeable HMM-LDA sequences, and topic-mixture recovery on 20Newsgroups and WikiText-103. This substantially extends coverage to mixed semantic/syntactic generation and natural language.

E2.justification: V2 adds explicit comparisons against BERT-tiny, LDA and a supervised word embedder in Table 3, plus comparisons among pretrained GPT-2, Llama 2 and BERT variants with a randomly initialized GPT-2 control. The retained HMM target comparisons are unchanged despite their new connection to belief-state inference.

E3.justification: The original three-layer toy-model configuration is retained. New protocols include a four-layer transformer for synthetic topics, pretrained-model evaluation with 20 or 100 LDA topics, total-variation loss, averaged versus last-token embeddings, and corpus-specific splits. Architecture sweeps additionally vary embedding width, depth and attention heads.

E4.justification: V2 adds cross-topic-model controls testing whether probes alone explain recovery, reverse prediction testing embedding parsimony, architecture sensitivity, Gamma-Exponential memorization tests, and layer/pooling analyses. It also examines semantic proportion in HMM-LDA and the topic–perplexity relationship while controlling for token position. Existing posterior-moment and Gaussian memorization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The retained HMM and rectangle tables switch from standard deviations to standard errors while still reporting ten seeds. New topic experiments and architecture sweeps report three-seed summaries. Appendix A.4 adds mixed-effects estimation with standard errors, degrees of freedom, p-values and a collinearity diagnostic, substantially expanding statistical analysis.

E6.justification: The HMM and rectangle table means remain unchanged, but v2 adds extensive results. Table 3 reports 70.5% AT versus 46.6% BERT accuracy at alpha = 1; Table 6 reports 28.4–84.6% embedding variance explained. Natural-corpus results and updated conjugate-model curves further expand the evidence. These are newly reported or replaced results, not established v1-to-v2 performance gains.

T1.justification: The original exchangeability proposition and proof remain. V2 Section 3.2 additionally establishes current-state posterior sufficiency alongside next-state posterior sufficiency through Equation 3. Appendix A.1 supplies Bayesian derivations for autoregressive and masked-language-model objectives, substantially extending the mathematical treatment.

C1.justification: V1's central claim concerns predictive sufficient statistics demonstrated through simple synthetic processes. V2's abstract and introduction extend the contribution to topic structure embedded in partially exchangeable sequences and pretrained language models on natural corpora. This materially broadens the claimed applicability while retaining the original framework.

C2.justification: V2 revises the HMM interpretation to acknowledge current-state sufficiency and explain next-state preference through output-layer computations. It adds interpretations concerning embedding parsimony, semantic proportion and masked-objective expressivity. V1's explicit limitations concerning simple likelihoods and hierarchical extensions are replaced by broader applications and future directions.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability link, new generative-process descriptions, corpus split sizes, model parameter counts, GPU assignments and tuning ranges with selected settings in Tables 9–12. Reproducibility information is substantially expanded, although Section 4.3's 100-word topic documents are not reconciled with Appendix A.3's general 500-token statement.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning relative to mechanistic interpretability, information-bottleneck theory, belief-state inference, mixed-membership concept extraction and concurrent Bayesian accounts. It adds discussions of Shai et al., Wang et al. and Ye et al., among others. V1's citation to Zhang et al. (2023), Deep de Finetti, is absent.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and discussion are extensively rewritten. Discrete hypotheses become a subsection of exchangeable models, their experiments merge into Section 4.1, Gaussian posterior-moment material moves to the appendix, and the conclusion becomes a separate section. This is substantial restructuring of retained material as well as expansion.

P2.justification: V2 merges rectangle schematics and selected PCA panels into Figure 3, relocates and rearranges v1's Gaussian-moment Figure 3 as appendix Figure 8, and redraws retained plots. New heatmaps, topic-mixture plots, an HMM-LDA illustration and numerous result/settings tables substantially change the visual presentation, alongside the journal layout.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses an important limitation of v1's entirely synthetic validation by testing pretrained models on natural corpora and adding controls for probe-driven explanations. Reverse prediction, the position-controlled statistical analysis and the HMM theoretical clarification strengthen the argument. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, including inconsistent topic-sequence lengths, the loss of explicit limitations, and Table 7's autoregressive-superiority caption conflicting with some accuracy entries.
